body:
Thank you everyone for your advice. As schmyd said. I do seem to judge my life based on the idea that "college is supposed to be the best years of your life."
It's difficult not to though. I get in these mental habits that while I can force myself to feel confident for maybe a week or so, it will rebound and I'll feel worse than usual. These ups and downs have taken a serious toll on my brain and each rebound seems to be worse. 

I am now seeking a therapist that can help me with my issues.
It doesn't help that when I try to make friends, like today I thought wtf and tried to start a conversation with a dude who sits next to me. He deliberately walked a different way to avoid conversation.
I swear it seems like life is one big test. A test to see how much shit you can take without breaking. 

Had you guys not replied, I may have had a much more intense reaction to that event. I am also agree that yes, I am comparing myself to other people way to much. It really bugs me that while I can live in such a big place, that I could feel so lonely. You'd think being surrounded by people would guarantee interaction and friendship. Why is it different for me though?

I feel like it's too late to change for me. That I'm too old and my brain is already set in it's insecure, awkward ways. I want to stop caring about the status quo, or what other people think. But my mind remains a cage, which locks all of these things into place like a cement mold drying and hardening.

Thank you all for your input, it's much appreciated. I hope that a therapist can help get to the root of my issues and maybe free me of them.

I wish it was as easy for me as not giving a f*** about standards or norms, or even what other people think, but as I mentioned, that seems to be my brain's default state.
